Seminar Title:

Determination of operational inclusion criteria (OIC) for diesel operated vehicles in underground hard rock mines considering DPM emission as key indicator

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Mining Engineering

Speaker Name:

Dr. Falguni Sarkar

Speaker Type:

Faculty

Venue:

Mining Department Seminar Hall

Date and Time:

15 Oct 2026 5:45 pm

Contact:

6204641962

Abstract:

Diesel-powered heavy earth moving machineries and other underground vehicles are widely used in underground hard rock mines due to their power, reliability and productivity. These include Load Haul Dumpers (LHDs), Low Profile Dump Trucks (LPDTs), Jumbo drills, rock bolters, excavators, passenger carriers, scissor lifters, explosive vans and other underground vehicles. However, the combustion of diesel fuel releases different exhaust emissions, including Diesel Particulate Matter (DPM), which poses a significant health risk to miners. DPM, by and large, consists of very small/micro particles (less than 1 µm in diameter) including carbon compounds, sulphates and metals, which can penetrate deep into the respiratory system and cause various diseases. Controlling and reducing DPM levels in underground hard rock mines are thus crucial to safeguard the occupational health and well-being of miners. In this study, DPM emission patterns of underground diesel-operated vehicles were assessed during loading/operational activities across underground mine workplaces having different ventilation scenarios. Surface DPM emission (SDE), underground average DPM emission and Operator’s DPM Dose (ODD) values obtained on an 8-hour TWA basis were recorded. Air velocity, temperature and humidity were also measured at the mine workplaces. Simple linear regression and multivariate regression analyses were carried out to determine the strength and pattern of interrelationship between SDE, ODD, air velocity, temperature and humidity. Based on the derived empirical equations, Surface DPM Emission (SDE) thresholds were quantified for different ventilation scenarios to restrict operator exposure below the statutory limit of 100 µg EC/m³. These thresholds provide the basis for Operational Inclusion Criteria (OIC) for diesel-operated underground vehicles, supporting controlled exposure, safer vehicle deployment and science-based asset management.
